result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter is from the hospital when you went home. The hospital says you have a urinary tract infection. The letter gives you a medicine called nitrofurantoin.

The letter has two different numbers of tablets. One part says 2 tablets each time. Another part says 1 tablet each time. The letter does not say which is right.

## What you need to do
1. Ask the hospital, your GP or your pharmacist how many tablets to take each time. Do this before you take the medicine.
2. The medicine is taken twice a day for 3 days.

## Dates and medicines
- Date you left the hospital: 24 September 2026
- Medicine: nitrofurantoin, 50 mg tablets (50 milligrams each)
- How often: twice a day for 3 days
- Number of tablets each time: unclear. One part of the letter says 2 tablets. Another part says 1 tablet.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- How many nitrofurantoin tablets should I take each time?
- What does urinary tract infection mean?
- Can you check the letter and tell me which number is right?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
